overview: This bill, the Black Vulture Relief Act, lets livestock producers and their employees capture, kill or scare off black vultures that are harming or that they reasonably believe will harm their livestock, without the federal permit normally required under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, a law that protects most native bird species. Using poison would be prohibited. Anyone who takes black vultures this way would have to file a yearly report with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, which must create a simple reporting form within 180 days. As of October 3, 2025, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say black vultures can attack and kill newborn calves and other livestock, and that farmers shouldn't have to wait for a federal permit to protect their animals.
against: Critics say letting people kill a protected bird without a permit weakens the oversight that the Migratory Bird Treaty Act provides, and relies on self-reporting after the fact to track how many birds are killed.
